A candid realistic photograph of an early-twenties Korean woman begging in a crowded Gaehwagi-era street, while a passerby throws her a half-eaten hamburger and a different passerby captures the moment; use the attached portrait for visible appearance.

A candid, photorealistic street photograph in a crowded Korean Gaehwagi-era commercial district during the opening-to-modernity period. At the center, a Korean woman in her early twenties with a fair milky complexion begs beside the dusty roadway, seated low with one bent knee and both feet grounded. Use the attached portrait only as the visual reference for her visible face, dark eyes, and dark chin-length bob with wispy bangs. Her worn period clothing is visibly smeared with dust and street grime; faint dirt marks cross her cheeks while her recognizable facial features remain clear. Her shoulders hunch, and her right hand reaches forward palm up in a pleading gesture while her left hand braces against the ground. She looks toward a passing pedestrian with a sorrowful, vulnerable expression. The passing pedestrian at frame left has just thrown a half-eaten hamburger toward her: the open throwing hand, the burger with an irregular bitten edge suspended in the air, and her reaching hand form one readable diagonal trajectory. Keep the anachronistic hamburger visibly distinct within the period street scene. Shopfronts, mixed traditional and early modern street dress, carts, and moving pedestrians make the district feel busy. Frame it from the viewpoint of a separate passerby who quickly raised a camera while walking, with a slightly tilted, imperfect crop, natural daylight, real street texture, and subtle background motion blur.
